name: implementation leakage
wording: realization showing through text that should state meaning: a concept, decision or example that names code, files, commands, flags, identifiers, tools or libraries instead of what must hold; it is flagged mechanically in the conceptual design as a warning the architect sees, not a gate, because a word list cannot tell every legitimate use from a leak.
reason: The architect repeatedly let mechanism into conceptual answers and briefs; requirements engineering names this implementation leakage and detects it with lexical rules (as in requirements-smell detection), useful as warnings because of their false positives.
